subject: 0 width/ or single pixel rectangle disappear, bad and good practice?

messages.author: 427356d65a15c6cc
messages.subject: 0 width/ or single pixel rectangle disappear, bad and good practice?
parts:
Dear list, 

Here is an example addressing my concern.

library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
       x = sample(1e5, 20, replace = TRUE),
       y = 10
     )

## nothing for sure 
ggplot(df, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x, ymin = y, ymax = y + 2)) +
    geom_rect()

## depends on scale
ggplot(df, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 1, ymin = y, ymax = y + 2)) +
    geom_rect()

## may show up some 
ggplot(df, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 10, ymin = y, ymax = y + 2)) +
    geom_rect()
 
when width of rectangle is 0, nothing will shown. even when it's 1, it's depends on the scale I guess, if the scale is too large, sometimes it doesn't show. This is misleading in my case when I am trying to map plot to my data. I should observe 20 cases on the plot.

For example, when I produce a set of random integer interval, where width of intervals are >= 1,  NOTICE: in bioconductor, IRanges represent basic inteval, so if start = 100  and end = 100, the width is 1 not 0! And genome space could over 1 billion, in this case
  1. my start = end case where I expect a *segment* will disappear for sure.
  2. small width my disappear due to large space
is it possible that 
  • regardless of the width, even start = end or any width, always show a segment behind? it's my hack for now, but maybe not general 
  • maybe more better solution?
Thanks

Tengfei

parts:
Hi

It looks like explicitly setting colors could solve the problem, default color is NA (as Hadley pointed for me). It's just if users are not aware of this, they may not be aware that they are missing observation, but since set color to non-transparent will have some other problems, as long as I got the solution, it's fine for me :)

Thanks again

Tengfei
